reason: J.B. Hunt earns service fees by moving freight for shippers (intermodal, dedicated trucking, brokerage, last-mile). Trinity leases and manufactures railcars and maintains them. Both work in North American rail-linked freight, but Trinity supplies equipment and does not run freight moves. Its main customers are railroads, lessors and rail shippers that own or lease railcars. J.B. Hunt's customers buy transportation services. The shared "shipper" label is too thin to count as real overlap.
reason_if_0: Different business model: Trinity is a railcar lessor and manufacturer with maintenance services. J.B. Hunt is a asset-and-brokerage freight transportation service provider that is paid per load or contract.
